---
order: 8
unit: capstone
title: "Capstone: your own AI sorter"
summary: Choose a sorting problem, build a fair test set first, train and improve a Pattern Trainer model until every group passes, connect a micro:bit build that acts safely on its labels, and report what it still gets wrong.
language: makecode
explainPicture: build.ts#sol-build
hook: "Engineers who build an AI system are asked two questions before it is used: how did you test it, and when does it fail? This time the problem, the data and the answers are yours."
---
You have trained a model, tested it fairly, fixed it by changing its data, and sent its labels to a micro:bit. Now do it all on a problem **you choose**, in four milestones with less help each time.

Some ideas: **ripe or unripe** fruit; **LEGO** bricks by colour or size; **tidy or messy** desk; **book or not a book**; **wet or dry** washing (photos only); a **recycling** sorter for your school's own bins. Two to four classes, plus a **Neither** class for everything else.

## Plan

```step
stage: info
check: { type: reflect, text: "I wrote down my problem, my classes (including Neither), where the model will be used, and what the micro:bit does for each label." }
```

Write in your book or a document:

1. The **problem** and who it helps.
2. The **classes** (with exact names, as you will type them in the Pattern Trainer), including **Neither**.
3. **Where** it will be used: the background, the light, the distance. These become your test groups.
4. What the **micro:bit** does for each label, and what it does when it is **unsure**.

## Milestone 1: build the test set first

```step
stage: modify
insight: "A fair test is made before training, from photos the model will never train on, taken in the conditions where it will be used."
try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#photos", height: 760 }
check: { type: board, text: "Add at least 24 test photos in at least 3 groups, with every class in every group.", when: "n_photos >= 24 and n_groups >= 3" }
```

Take your **test photos before you train**, and keep them apart from your training photos. For each class, take photos in **at least three groups**: different places, light or distances where the model will be used. On the board, choose the class, name the group, then **Add photos**. (The photos stay in this browser only.)

## Milestone 2: train, test, improve

```step
stage: modify
insight: "Improving means finding the weakest group and changing the training data for it, not just raising the overall score."
try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#photos", height: 760 }
check: { type: board, text: "Get 80% or more overall, with no group below 60%.", when: "acc_all >= 0.8 and acc_min >= 0.6" }
```

Train in the [Pattern Trainer](https://tools.learningwaypoints.com/trainer/) (new photos, not your test photos), click **Download my_model.json**, and open it here with **Open your model file**. Find the **weakest group**, work out what its failures share, change the training data, and test again. Keep a note of each change and its scores.

## Milestone 3: the build

```step
stage: make
try: { playground: microbit, starter: "build.ts#start" }
check: { type: code, text: "The micro:bit acts on each of your labels, does something safe for anything else (Unsure, Neither, or a word it doesn't know), and replies with what it did.", rules: { inside: { "serial.onDataReceived": ["serial.readLine()", "if(label==", "}else{", "serial.writeValue("] } } }
```

Program the micro:bit: one branch for each of your labels, an **else** that does something safe, and a **reply** (serial write value) saying what it did. A servo flap, lights, a sound or the screen: your choice. If the build is across the room, add the radio bridge.

## Milestone 4: the whole system

```step
stage: run
tier: typical
try: { playground: board, starter: "boards.yml#system", height: 760 }
check: { type: board, text: "Run the whole system: at least 5 labels sent from the webcam and 5 replies from the micro:bit.", when: "n_sent >= 5 and n_replies >= 5" }
```

Load your model, connect your micro:bit, and run it on the webcam with real items. Watch what happens when you show something that is in no class at all.

## Report

```step
stage: info
check: { type: reflect, text: "I wrote my report: the problem, my test set, my scores by group before and after, what I changed, what it still gets wrong, and who or what it might fail for." }
```

Write a one-page report (or a two-minute talk):

- The **problem** and your **classes**.
- Your **test set**: groups and how many photos.
- **Scores by group**, first and final, and **what you changed** in the data each time.
- What the micro:bit does, including when the model is **unsure**.
- What it **still gets wrong**, and **who or what it might fail for** if a real person relied on it.

```teacher
summary: Students build an AI sorter for a problem they choose, in four
  milestones (test set, model, build, system), and report its scores by group
  and its limits.
time: 120
timing: "About two to three lessons: Plan 15 min · Test set 20 min · Train and
  improve 35 min · Build 25 min · System 10 min (typical) · Report 15 min"
goals:
  - I can build a fair test set before training, with groups for the conditions
    where the model will be used.
  - I can improve a model by changing its data for its weakest group.
  - I can make a build act safely on a model's labels and report what it still
    gets wrong.
before: >
  **The capstone** brings the course together on a problem each student (or
  pair) chooses. The order matters: **test set first**, from photos the model
  never trains on, in groups that match where it will be used (place, light,
  distance). The board keeps the test photos **in the student's browser only**
  (testset: own); they are shrunk to small squares and never uploaded. Remind
  students not to photograph people.


  **Training:** in the Pattern Trainer; students open the downloaded
  `my_model.json` on the board after each retrain. **Teachable Machine still
  works:** a student who trains there can export with **Upload my model** and
  paste the link into the box under **Open your model file**. Its webcam is
  mirrored; the Pattern Trainer's is not.


  **Milestones:** (1) at least 24 test photos in at least 3 groups; (2) 80%
  overall with no group under 60% (the board's acc_min); (3) a micro:bit program
  with a branch per label, a safe else and a reply; (4) the whole system on the
  webcam (typical: needs a micro:bit). The report is the assessment piece:
  scores by group before and after, the data changes made, and the limits.


  **Choosing problems:** steer away from people (faces, emotions, who someone
  is) and anything where a wrong answer could hurt someone. Good problems have
  objects students can bring in. Two to four classes plus Neither is plenty.


  **Without micro:bits:** milestones 1, 2 and 3 work without hardware (3 is
  checked in the editor); milestone 4 is typical.
running:
  - "Plan: check class names are exact and that every class has a Neither
    alternative."
  - "Test set: check groups are real conditions (window, desk, dim), not just
    more of the same."
  - "Improve: ask each student which group is weakest and what its failures
    share."
  - "Build: the safe else is the AI robots idea in a new setting."
  - "Report: ask 'who or what might it fail for?' of every report."
stuck:
  - see: The test score is 100% straight away.
    ask: Are any test photos also training photos? Are your groups different enough?
    fix: Retake test photos apart from training ones, in harder conditions.
  - see: One group stays low however much is added.
    ask: Do the new training photos look like that group's test photos?
    fix: Take training photos in that group's conditions.
  - see: The board loses the test photos.
    ask: Are you in the same browser and not in a private window?
    fix: Use the same browser profile; private windows forget them.
stretch: Add a second model in CreateAI (a movement) that starts or stops the
  sorter, so the two models work together.
support: Offer a ready-made problem (the recycling sorter with your school's
  bins) and a planning template with the four plan questions.
leads: "Where this leads: AI robots (a robot driven by a model, with safety
  rules), and the Python pathway's Machine learning with Gradio. Real world:
  model cards and test reports for AI systems."
exit:
  q: Why build the test set before training?
  a: "So it holds photos the model never trained on, from the conditions where it
    will be used: a fair test of whether it works there."
explain: >
  Build your AI sorter in four milestones:


  1. **Test set first**: photos the model never trains on, in groups for where
  it will be used.

  2. **Train and improve**: fix the **weakest group** by changing the data.

  3. **Build**: act on each label, do something **safe** for anything else, and
  reply.

  4. **Report**: scores by group, what you changed, and what it still gets
  wrong.
solutions:
  step-4: build.ts#sol-build
struggle: Making the test set before training and keeping it separate. When the
  score is 100% at once, ask whether any test photos were also training photos.
```
